purpose: Determine whether the already-existing Azami image dataset can serve as prospective held-out confirmation of the EAzami orientation transition-climate discovery.
reasons: Azami already analyzed the same orientation endpoint against the same nine-variable climate universe, including within-taxon models; reusing BIO1/BIO15 now would be post-result, not held-out.
The Azami endpoint is an image-referenced presentation angle, not a gravity-referenced botanical head-orientation measurement.
Existing within-taxon BIO1 and BIO15 directions do not reproduce the EAzami downward-transition discovery direction.

azami_endpoint.definition: signed PCA head axis relative to EXIF-oriented image vertical
azami_endpoint.biological_limit: not a direct gravity-referenced inclinometer angle or peduncle-deflection measurement

eazami_discovery.interpretation: phylogeny-conditioned transition-level present-niche correspondence; not historical climatic causation

BIO1.direction_given_angle_mapping: warmer -> larger angle -> more downward in image coordinates
BIO1.relation_to_eazami: opposite to EAzami D-associated lower BIO1

BIO15.direction_given_angle_mapping: higher precipitation seasonality -> smaller angle -> more upward in image coordinates
BIO15.relation_to_eazami: directionally opposite to EAzami D-associated higher BIO15; not FDR-supported

BIO12.interpretation: strong existing among-taxon anchor; different estimand and predictor from EAzami BIO15/BIO1 transition vector

inference.cross_scale_result: orientation-environment correspondence is scale/representation dependent rather than a simple repeated sign across taxonomic levels
inference.allowed_use: existing complementary cross-scale evidence and Discussion-level boundary
prohibited_use: proof that EAzami transition signal generalizes within taxa
proof of adaptation or climatic causation

next_validation: aza3 gravity-referenced field orientation manipulation/measurement with preregistered wetting/temperature/pollination/fitness pathways
